title: Stirred mesh gradient

reference.source: Yoo Sung Lee, published to the mmeshy community gallery; mmeshy is a free mesh-gradient editor by Isaiah Trotter
reference.grammar: soft color sources on a canvas, no stops; a grain pass; the editor’s own blend mode and softness

units: frame widths; the frame is 1 wide and 0.521 tall; v on the plate is y / 0.521

ground.colour: none; the sources cover the frame

techniques.name: Gaussian pull

params.d: distance from the pixel to the source, in frame widths

techniques.implementation: Each source is a position, an OKLab color and a reach. Its weight at a pixel is a gaussian of the distance; nothing is clamped, so every source touches every pixel a little.

techniques.name: Line source with bow
techniques.implementation: A horizontal source is a parabola in u; the distance is vertical. The bow is what makes the bands rise toward the edges instead of running flat.

techniques.name: Normalized OKLab mix

params.normalize: weights divided by their sum, with the largest exponent factored out for precision
params.out: OKLab → linear sRGB → sRGB, plus 1/255 dither

techniques.implementation: The pixel is the weight-average of the thirteen OKLab colors; converting back to sRGB only at the end keeps the transitions out of gray.

techniques.name: Lightness grain

params.hash: fract(sin-free integer hash of the cell)
params.where: added to L before the sRGB conversion

techniques.implementation: A hashed value per 2-px cell nudges OKLab L up or down; since it rides on L it darkens and lightens without shifting hue.

techniques.name: Curl stir

params.note: the instrument stirs the field with two octaves of curl noise; the reference is unstirred, so this plate sets it to zero

techniques.implementation: When non-zero, the sample position is displaced by a divergence-free curl of value noise before the pulls are evaluated, so color is carried and never pinched.

coupling: One reach per source sets both how far its color travels and how soft its edge is; the two cannot be tuned apart, which is what keeps a mesh gradient from looking like stacked blobs.
inferred: the source kinds and bows: the editor shows handles, not the strokes they belong to
that the editor blends in a perceptual space; its Overlay mode and the filter pass are not reproduced

hand.drag a source: moves it; a line moves up and down; let go while moving and it glides
hand.drag the field: stirs; sources near the stroke are carried along
hand.scroll: on a source its reach, on the field the marbling, with the ring open the lightness
hand.hold: opens the ring: around for hue, outward for chroma; hold on the field to add a source

keys.l: turn a point into a line and back

controller.right_stick: angle is hue, throw is chroma

midi.note: turn six knobs in that order to claim them; any pad selects a source

notes: Seed 1010 for the grain hash offset.
Sources are tuned by eye against the reference in split view; the numbers under measured are what they were tuned to.
The editor’s node colors are listed under reference; the plate’s sources are the colors read from the rendered reference, which already carry the filter pass.
The spec drawer re-reads the live sources when it opens, so a stirred state can be copied out as JSON.
